title: 3.5.21 Plain English to Pseudocode: Destructuring vs. Plain Access
description: Turn four plain-English steps into pseudocode for describeBox(): unpack width, height and color from options in one step, build the note, add "(wide)" only when width is greater than height, then give the note back.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([describeBox starts]) --> B[unpack width, height and color from options]
  B --> C[build the note from color, width and height]
  C --> D{is width greater than height?}

steps.title: Turn the plain-English steps into pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is the plan in plain English:

**1.** Take `width`, `height` and `color` out of `options` in one step.

**2.** Build the note from the color, the width and the height.

**3.** If the width is greater than the height, the box is wide.

**4.** In that case, add `" (wide)"` to the end of the note.

**5.** Either way, give the note back.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor (open the Flow Chart bar). You do not draw it, you read it: the unpack is a box of its own at the start, and the diamond sits after the note is built.

In `README.md`, type these as numbered pseudocode **between the first and last line**. Number every line, including indented ones. Each keyword looks like this, in a different program:

- `SET lives TO 3` (start a value)
- `IF lives is 0` ... `END IF` (a check, with the steps inside it indented)
- `ADD 1 TO lives` (change a value)
- `RETURN lives` (the answer)

Plain English is fine here. Press **Grade** above the editor: the AI reads what your steps mean and marks each Quest card green or red. Changing your text clears its marks, so press Grade again when you have finished editing.

Before you submit, trace it twice by hand: once with width 10 and height 4, and once with width 3 and height 8. Only the first should reach the step that adds the word wide.
hints: Take all three values out of `options` in one line. Three lines that each read one field are the plain-access version of this program.
The check for wide comes after the note is built, and only the yes side adds to the note.

requirements.title: Numbered steps
requirements.description: Number your steps 1. 2. 3. and so on, with something written after each number.
requirements.hint: Write at least four lines that start with a number, each with a step written after it.

requirements.title: Unpacks all three values in one step
requirements.description: Take width, height and color out of options in a single step.
requirements.hint: Write one step that takes width, height and color out of options together, not one line per field.

requirements.title: The note is built after the unpack
requirements.description: Build the note after the values are out of options.
requirements.hint: Put the step that builds the note after the unpack step.

requirements.title: Asks whether width is greater than height
requirements.description: Check whether the width is greater than the height.
requirements.hint: Add a check that asks whether width is greater than height (not less than, and not equal).

requirements.title: The wide case adds to the note
requirements.description: Inside the check, add " (wide)" to the note.
requirements.hint: After the check, add a step that appends " (wide)" to the note.

requirements.title: The note is given back after the check
requirements.description: Give the note back after the decision, on both paths.
requirements.hint: Finish with a step that gives back the note, after the check.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your steps
aiCheck.prompt: The student was given plain-English steps and rewrote them as numbered, step-by-step pseudocode in README.md, between a first line and a last line that were already there. The program they were describing is describeBox(options): take width, height and color out of options in one step; build the note from color, width and height; if width is greater than height, add " (wide)" to the note; give the note back. Judge each criterion ONLY by whether its idea is present in the student's steps, however they word it. Plain English, keywords such as SET, IF, END IF, RETURN, or a mix of both are all fine, and so are different names, different capitalisation, and different ways to number the lines. Do not require any particular keyword. A step that is clearly aimed at the criterion is enough for 'met'. Mark a criterion 'missing' only when the idea is absent or the steps do the opposite, for example adding the wide text before the width test for the wide criterion. Write each note for THIS student's own steps: in a not-met note, name the exact step or word in their steps that causes the problem (quote at most a few words), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected steps. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their steps satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.

rubric.title: Numbered steps
rubric.description: The student numbered their steps (1. 2. 3. or similar), at least four of them.

rubric.title: Unpacks all three values in one step
rubric.description: One step takes width, height and color out of options together. If each field is read in its own step (options.width, options.height, ...), or the unpack never happens, mark this missing.

rubric.title: The note is built after the unpack
rubric.description: The step that builds the note (color, width and height joined into text) comes AFTER the unpack. If the note is built first, mark this missing.

rubric.title: Asks whether width is greater than height
rubric.description: The steps ask whether the width is greater than the height (or equivalently whether the box is wide). A flipped comparison (width less than height), an "or equal" test, or no check at all is missing.

rubric.title: The wide case adds to the note
rubric.description: When the width is greater than the height, a step adds " (wide)" (or the word wide) to the end of the note. If it is added before the check, or always, or never, mark this missing.

rubric.title: The note is given back after the check
rubric.description: After the check, the steps give back (return or print) the note. If it is given back before the check, or never, mark this missing.
